items.readable_text:
Content:
The slope-intercept form of the equation of a line is

Content:
[MATH: y = {\color{red}{m}}x+{\color{blue}{b}},]

Content:
where [MATH: {\color{red}{m}}] is the slope of the line and [MATH: {\color{blue}{b}}] is the [MATH: y]-intercept.

Content:
To illustrate, consider the line [MATH: y={\color{red}{2}}x+{\color{blue}{1}},] shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f816241b18e1a1ba1f9abcfdd6b78d76]

Content:
Looking at the line, we notice that:

Content:
- The slope of the line is [MATH: m={\color{red}{2}},] because a change of [MATH: 1] in the [MATH: x]-direction results in a change of [MATH: 2] in the [MATH: y]-direction.
- The [MATH: y]-intercept of the line, denoted [MATH: b], is [MATH: b={\color{blue}{1}},] because the line hits the [MATH: y]-axis at the point [MATH: (0,{\color{blue}{1}}).]

Content:
Note: The coordinates of the [MATH: y]-intercept are always [MATH: (0,{\color{blue}{b}}).]

Content:
Finally, if the slope [MATH: m = 0] (i.e., we have a horizontal line), the slope-intercept form must be [MATH: y=0x+{\color{blue}b},] which reduces to [MATH: y={\color{blue}b}.]

sections.normalized_html: The line shown above passes through the points [MATH: (0,-2)] and [MATH: (2,2).]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/2bdc5b12fe9582ecf98e8205de693e92]

The line shown above passes through the points [MATH: (0,-2)] and [MATH: (2,2).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form [MATH: y=mx+b.] So, we need to work out the slope [MATH: m] and the [MATH: y]-intercept [MATH: b.]

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the [MATH: y]-axis at [MATH: (0,-2).] So, the [MATH: y]-intercept is [MATH: b = -2.]

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points [MATH: (0,-2)] and [MATH: (2,2),] so we calculate its slope as follows: [MATH: m|= (y_{2} − y_{1})/(x_{2} − x_{1}); = (2 − (− 2))/(2 − 0); = (4)/(2); = 2]

Substituting the slope [MATH: m = 2] and the [MATH: y]-intercept [MATH: b = -2] into the slope-intercept form [MATH: y = mx + b,] we obtain the equation of the line: [MATH: y = 2x - 2.]
